payload.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image establish that the requested black DVD has become a white DVD?
node.criteria: Inspect the edited endpoint first, then compare with the source to establish which object the observation concerns. Pass if visible evidence establishes that the requested source DVD has a white edited counterpart identifiable as a DVD. Fail if a reliably matched counterpart visibly does not meet that endpoint. Unknown if target selection, correspondence, color, or DVD identity leaves completion unresolved. Identify the source object and edited counterpart and cite the scene relationships or object features supporting the match. The central printed rectangular source item is a candidate locator, not a required preserved case or silhouette. Consider the separate right-hand object without automatically treating it as the DVD. Whiteness alone does not prove correspondence, and changed shape alone does not disprove it. DVD identity may be supported by appearance and scene context; do not demand readable labels or a visually provable DVD-versus-CD distinction.
node.binding: The black DVD requested in the source image and its corresponding edited object, not any white object selected solely because it resembles a disc.

node_traces.evidence: The source’s central printed rectangular item is a plausible DVD case, while the separate right-hand object is a black disc-like item. In the edited image, the central item is gone and two white discs appear: one near the center and one over the right-hand object. The images do not establish which, if either, corresponds to the requested DVD, so the requested transformation cannot be confirmed or ruled out.

fulfillment: The binding is too vague and conflates the requested target with the DVD case: the source image shows a small printed rectangular item near center and a separate black disc-like object at right; the edit shows two white discs, one near center and one at right. Do not assume either white disc corresponds to the requested source DVD, but make the node explicitly compare the right-hand black disc with the edited right-hand white disc using position, shape, and scene context, and assess whether it remains identifiable as a DVD. The traces currently stop at uncertainty despite this plausible spatial correspondence; require a target-specific judgment that distinguishes actual whitening from unrelated added objects, while retaining unknown if correspondence or DVD identity genuinely cannot be established. Keep the existing partial/absent criteria and do not infer absence merely from the missing central item or from uncertainty. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated; this is a visual binding/evidence-resolution issue.
s2: Improve the binding and evidence instructions to distinguish the small central printed rectangular item from the separate black disc-like object on the right in the source. Compare the right-hand source object with the right-hand edited disc using location, shape, and scene context; do not treat the central edited white disc as the target merely because it is white. Require an explicit target-correspondence and color-change judgment, including whether the right-hand object shows any black-to-white surface change and whether it remains identifiable as a DVD. Preserve the existing pass/fail/unknown and partial-progress criteria: unrelated added objects are not progress, but do not label no progress solely because correspondence or identity is uncertain. The trace is a valid visual uncertainty, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure; resolve the plausible spatial match from image evidence without forcing a conclusion.
